editorial.marketOverview: Friday's technology-led decline remained severe in the latest timestamped observations available from the prior assessment. Reuters separately described global risk aversion and heavy semiconductor selling. Because official 16:00 ET closes could not be independently established, the late-session intraday readings must not be represented as final closes.
editorial.whatChanged: This manual post-session review advances the horizon to Monday November 23 through Wednesday November 25 and adds the holiday-shortened week's earnings and macro calendar. It does not establish a new synchronized market move or new curated Open Watch catalyst. Directional bias is unchanged.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor underperformance and elevated volatility support a defensive three-day baseline. Earlier 10Y 4.94% and 2Y 4.65% imply +29 basis points, not 0.29 basis points, but are not current synchronized measurements. Reuters described Treasury safe-haven demand; it cannot by itself confirm a sustained technology rebound. The exact role of regulatory and AI valuation headlines in Friday's prices is unproven.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday may see downside continuation or a sharp mechanical oversold bounce; Tuesday's chip leadership and market breadth will determine whether any bounce holds. Wednesday brings concentrated 08:30 ET macro releases and the Fed Beige Book, increasing event-driven two-way risk. No numeric price targets are justified without verified closing prices and current volatility.
editorial.bullCase: A tradable recovery would require QQQ and SOX/SMH stabilizing together, breadth improving and volatility retreating. Treasury yield relief and an oversold technical setup are potential supports, not confirmed reversal evidence.
editorial.bearCase: Severe prior intraday QQQ/NVDA weakness, reported chip-sector losses and high volatility leave the market vulnerable to further liquidation. A failed Monday rebound or continued chip underperformance would reinforce downside continuation.
